42932003.title: GLP-1 receptor agonist-associated weight loss in breast cancer patients receiving concurrent endocrine therapy: a retrospective cohort analysis
quotes: We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of 269 breast cancer patients at a single academic center receiving concurrent GLP-1 RA and adjuvant endocrine therapy.

Mean one-year percentage weight loss was - 4.5% (95% CI: -6.0% to - 3.0%; -3.9 kg; 95% CI: -4.96 to - 2.93 kg), significantly below the 10-20% observed in postmenopausal subgroups of GLP-1 randomized trials (all p < 0.001).
Only 21.3% achieved ≥ 10% and 10.4% achieved ≥ 15% weight loss.
semaglutide (- 5.8%) and tirzepatide (- 4.7%) outperformed dulaglutide (+ 0.1%), which is approved for type 2 diabetes only.
PR-negative patients lost more than PR-positive patients (- 8.2% vs. -4.2%; p = 0.021, d = 0.46).
Type 2 diabetes was present in 70.6% of patients
Given emerging evidence of oncologic benefit, prospective trials are needed.

42906947.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Cancer Risk in Obesity Treatment
quotes: To date, data suggest that GLP-1 RAs do not increase overall cancer risk and may reduce the risk of certain obesity-related cancers
questions remain about the beneficial effects of weight loss and the sustainability of health benefits if weight is regained after stopping treatment
specific safety concerns (e.g., increased risk of medullary thyroid carcinoma)

41359966.title: Risk for Cancer With Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Dual Agonists : A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
quotes: The review included 48 trials involving 94 245 participants.

GLP-1RAs probably have little or no effect on risk for thyroid cancer (OR, 1.37 [95% CI, 0.82 to 2.31]; 1 fewer to 9 more cases per 10 000 patients treated), pancreatic cancer (OR, 0.84 [CI, 0.53 to 1.35]; 9 fewer to 6 more per 10 000), breast cancer (OR, 0.95 [CI, 0.60 to 1.49]; 10 fewer to 12 more per 10 000), or kidney cancer (OR, 1.12 [CI, 0.78 to 1.60]; 5 fewer to 13 more per 10 000) (moderate certainty).
GLP-1RAs may have little or no effect on colorectal, esophageal, liver, gallbladder, ovarian, or endometrial cancer; multiple myeloma; or meningioma (low certainty).
The effect on gastric cancer is very uncertain.
Results were consistent in sensitivity analyses of trials with low risk of bias and studies of semaglutide or tirzepatide
The included trials were not designed to evaluate cancer outcomes and had short follow-up.
Longer-term studies are needed to clarify potential risks or benefits. None. (PROSPERO: CRD42024608365).

40437949.title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and the risk for cancer: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
quotes: Fifty trials were included.
GLP-1RA treatment was not associated with a significant difference in risk for overall cancer (MH-OR 1.05, 95% confidence interval [CI] [0.98, 1.13]).

Uterine cancer was significantly reduced in the GLP-1RA arm in trials performed in subjects with obesity (MH-OR 0.24, 95% CI [0.06, 0.94]), but not in those aimed at diabetes treatment (MH-OR 0.92, [0.58, 1.47]).

We detected an increase in the risk for thyroid cancer (MH-OR 1.55, [1.05, 2.27]), more evident in longer-term trials, and in the risk for colorectal cancer (MH-OR 1.27 [1.03, 1.57]), which, conversely, was significant only in shorter-term trials.
the small increase observed in colorectal cancer in shorter-term trials may be the effect of a disproportionate increase in diagnostic procedures in the GLP-1 RA arm

41189318.title: Weight Loss, Obesity Medication, and Risk of Obesity-Associated Cancer: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
quotes: The analysis included 25 randomized controlled trials with 40,731 participants.
Compared with placebo, AOMs showed no association with the risk of overall obesity-related cancer (RR = 1.03, 95% CI: 0.78 to 1.37) or site-specific cancer.
subgroup analysis revealed that coagonists (tirzepatide, cotadutide, and cagrilintide) significantly reduced overall obesity-associated cancer risk (RR = 0.43, 95% CI: 0.19 to 0.97)

42221413.title: Incretin-Based Therapy and Thyroid Cancer Risk: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
quotes: Fifteen RCTs enrolling 84 237 participants were included.
Across all trials, 28 thyroid cancer events occurred in the incretin-based therapy groups and 15 in the control groups.
Meta-analysis showed no statistically significant association between incretin-based therapy use and thyroid cancer risk (odds ratio 1.52, 95% CI 0.86-2.68; I2 = 0.0%).
Certainty of evidence was rated very low due to serious imprecision related to rare events.
limited follow-up and imprecision prevent exclusion of a clinically relevant increase, supporting the need for long-term surveillance.

38018310.title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and risk of thyroid cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
quotes: We retrieved 64 trials, 26 of which reported at least one incident case of thyroid cancer.

GLP-1RA treatment was associated with a significant increase in the risk of overall thyroid cancer (Mantel-Haenzel odds ratio [MH-OR] 1.52 [95% confidence interval {CI} 1.01, 2.29]; P = 0.04, I2 = 0%), with a fragility index of 1, and a 5-year number needed to harm of 1349.
No significant association was found for papillary thyroid cancer (MH-OR 1.54 [95% CI 0.77, 3.06]; P = 0.22) or medullary thyroid cancer (MH-OR 1.44 [95% CI 0.23, 9.16]; P = 0.55).

38683947.title: Glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist use and risk of thyroid cancer: Scandinavian cohort study
quotes: 76 of 145 410 patients (incidence rate 1.33 events per 10 000 person years) treated with GLP1 receptor agonists and 184 of 291 667 patients (incidence rate 1.46 events per 10 000 person years) treated with DPP4 inhibitors developed thyroid cancer.

GLP1 receptor agonist use was not associated with increased risk of thyroid cancer (hazard ratio 0.93, 95% confidence interval 0.66 to 1.31; rate difference -0.13, 95% confidence interval -0.61 to 0.36 events per 10 000 person years).
The hazard ratio for medullary thyroid cancer was 1.19 (0.37 to 3.86).

36356111.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and the Risk of Thyroid Cancer
quotes: A total of 2,562 case subjects with thyroid cancers were included in the study and matched with 45,184 control subjects.

Use of GLP-1 RA for 1-3 years was associated with increased risk of all thyroid cancer (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.58, 95% CI 1.27-1.95) and medullary thyroid cancer (adjusted HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.04-3.05).

42252247.title: GLP-1 receptor agonist use and cancer risk in obese nondiabetic adults
quotes: Patients prescribed GLP-1RAs were 1:1 propensity score matched to those receiving diet or exercise counseling
the study cohort included 161 798 patients: 80 899 GLP-1RA users versus 80 899 patients on diet or exercise consultation.

With a median follow-up of 2 years (interquartile range 1-2 years), the propensity score matching analysis showed a significantly lower incidence of any OACs among GLP-1RA users (hazard ratio 0.59, 95% confidence interval 0.53-0.67).
in all subgroups, except for black race, GLP-1RA use was associated with a lower cumulative incidence of OACs.
Prospective trials are needed to confirm causality.

38967919.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide 1 Receptor Agonists and 13 Obesity-Associated Cancers in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes
quotes: GLP-1RAs compared with insulin were associated with a significant risk reduction in 10 of 13 OACs
GLP-1RAs were not associated with a reduced risk of postmenopausal breast cancer or thyroid cancer.
Compared with metformin, GLP-1RAs were not associated with a decreased risk of any cancers, but were associated with an increased risk of kidney cancer (HR, 1.54; 95% CI, 1.27-1.87).

40903861.title: Weight loss interventions and obesity-associated cancers in people with type 2 diabetes and overweight/obesity: A real-world observational study
quotes: In 64,178 matched pairs (mean follow-up 911 days), semaglutide (vs. DPP-4i) was associated with lower rates of composite OAC (HR: 0.88; 95% CI: 0.82-0.95)
tirzepatide (vs. DPP-4i) was associated with a non-significant lower rate of composite OAC (0.84; 0.69-1.01)

42447648.title: Cancer risk of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists for obesity: comparison with bariatric surgery and other weight-loss drugs
quotes: Compared with bariatric surgery, therapeutic-dose GLP-1 RA use was associated with a lower incidence of CRC (hazard ratio [HR], 0.72; P =.038) and pancreatic cancer (HR, 0.63; P =.041), but not HCC.
The use of any dose was not associated with significant differences.

quotes: Using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, we identified women with overweight or obesity who initiated tirzepatide (study group) or lifestyle modification interventions (control group) between January 1, 2022, and December 31, 2025.
Tirzepatide use was associated with a lower short-term hazard of newly recorded EC diagnoses among women with overweight or obesity.
After matching, 176,981 patients were included in each group.
tirzepatide use was associated with a lower hazard of newly recorded EC diagnoses compared with the comparator cohort (HR, 0.717; 95% CI, 0.593–0.867)
These observational findings do not establish a preventive effect, and longer-term studies are needed to assess whether the association persists.

wegovy_quotes: In rodents, semaglutide causes dose-dependent and treatment-duration-dependent thyroid C-cell tumors at clinically relevant exposures.

It is unknown whether WEGOVY causes thyroid C-cell tumors, including medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), in humans as human relevance of semaglutide-induced rodent thyroid C-cell tumors has not been determined
WEGOVY is contraindicated in patients with a personal or family history of MTC or in patients with Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2)
inform them of symptoms of thyroid tumors (e.g., a mass in the neck, dysphagia, dyspnea, persistent hoarseness).
Routine monitoring of serum calcitonin or using thyroid ultrasound is of uncertain value for early detection of MTC in patients treated with WEGOVY

analysis.note: Jabbit analysis. Pooled randomized trials (not designed for cancer, short follow-up) show little or no effect of GLP-1 drugs on most obesity-related cancers, with a possible thyroid signal that is imprecise and conflicts with a large Scandinavian cohort. Health-record studies report fewer cancers on GLP-1 drugs, but results depend on the comparison group and follow-up is short, so they cannot show prevention. Registered cancer trials of tirzepatide we found are small, mostly single-arm, and none is placebo-controlled.
